NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI compute value chain as a fabless semiconductor designer, relying critically on TSMC for cutting-edge GPU fabrication and SK Hynix for HBM memory, while selling the industry's dominant AI accelerators to the world's largest hyperscalers and cloud providers. Its chokepoint position in AI infrastructure—with no near-term alternative for high-performance GPU training clusters—gives it exceptional pricing power downstream and significant concentration risk upstream tied to TSMC's advanced nodes.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly complex global supply chain, acting as a 'fabless' designer of its own silicon and a systems integrator that sources hundreds of specialized components from suppliers across Asia, Europe, and North America. On the demand side, Apple sells primarily direct-to-consumer through its retail and online stores, but relies heavily on wireless carriers for subsidized iPhone distribution and on platform partners like Google for high-margin Services revenue, making it both a powerful supply chain orchestrator and a critical revenue driver for dozens of upstream and downstream partners.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron sits at the center of the memory and storage value chain, heavily dependent on a small group of specialized capital equipment suppliers — particularly ASML, Applied Materials, and Lam Research — for the advanced lithography and etch tools needed to manufacture DRAM and NAND at leading-edge nodes. On the demand side, Micron's revenue is increasingly driven by AI infrastructure buildout, making hyperscalers and GPU vendors like NVIDIA (for HBM) its most critical and fastest-growing customers, while consumer electronics OEMs and cloud providers provide broad diversification across its product portfolio.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: ARM Holdings occupies a uniquely asset-light position as a pure-play IP licensor sitting at the very foundation of the semiconductor ecosystem, generating revenue through royalties and licensing fees rather than physical manufacturing. Its upstream dependencies are primarily EDA software vendors and cloud infrastructure providers, while its downstream reach spans virtually every major semiconductor company globally, making it a critical intellectual chokepoint for mobile, data center, automotive, and IoT computing.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology is a fabless semiconductor company heavily reliant on TSMC for advanced-node manufacturing and Arm for IP licensing, positioning it as a critical middleware provider between leading-edge chip fabrication and hyperscale cloud infrastructure. On the downstream side, Marvell is increasingly exposed to major cloud titans (AWS, Google, Meta) through custom ASIC co-design engagements for AI/ML and networking, while also serving traditional OEM enterprise customers in storage and networking.
